actual_review_method: This same independent reviewer read the raw sources and froze phases1/2/3/v2 before viewing current v2 source and anonymous reconstruction, then compared all seven slots; decisions below are authored reviewer judgments, not a replay or generated verdict.

objects.original: One real random square matrix X on (Omega,Sigma,mu); ordinary X squared; actual Bochner expectations and matrix exponential.
objects.reconstructed: Same X and probability experiment; entry expansions of X squared; V=E X squared, alpha(s)=exp(s)-s-1 and M_s are explicit abbreviations; exp is the full matrix power series.
objects.evidence: Packet source original_text and reconstruction objects sections agree. P46-58 and the frozen Mathlib definitions establish matrix product, matrix exponential and actual integral meanings; no entrywise substitute appears.

domains.original: Probability measure on an arbitrary measurable space; real matrices on a finite nonempty index; Euclidean operator-norm topology; s real and positive.
domains.reconstructed: Arbitrary measurable Omega, probability mu, finite decidable nonempty I, n>=1, real square matrices and real s>0, with the same topology.
domains.evidence: The source is explicitly the real finite-positive-dimension restriction of Tropp Lemma6.7, not a complete complex-carrier port. The decoder retains that carrier and introduces no positivity or lower-spectrum domain restriction.

quantifiers.original: For every experiment, finite nonempty index and admissible X, for every s>0 the full PSD conclusion holds.
quantifiers.reconstructed: Same outer universal quantifiers and every positive s; PSD expands to every real test vector; separate a.e. hypotheses may have separate null exceptional sets.
quantifiers.evidence: P47-58 fixes X and mu before the positive parameter. The reconstruction does not turn the expectation theorem into a pointwise omega assertion, fix a chosen s, or lose the universal quadratic-form quantifier.

assumptions.original: A.e. strong measurability, Bochner integrable X and ordinary X squared, a.e. symmetry, a.e. X<=I, actual EX=0, s>0.
assumptions.reconstructed: The same explicit seven conditions, with no added independence, distribution, PSD X, lower spectral bound, norm cap or exponential-integrability input.
assumptions.evidence: P50-56 exactly supplies these binders. Tropp2.2 supports the explicit standing regularity, and the source/decoder both distinguish the one-sided cap from ||X||<=1. P69-72 derives exponential integrability internally.

conclusion.original: exp((exp(s)-s-1) integral X squared)-integral exp(sX) is positive semidefinite.
conclusion.reconstructed: The identical full PSD matrix difference, including symmetry and every quadratic form; equivalently E exp(sX)<=exp((exp(s)-s-1)E X squared).
conclusion.evidence: Order direction, actual second moment, coefficient and full matrix sense match P57-58 and the raw Tropp pp25-26 formula. No trace, scalar proxy, tail probability, sum or dimension factor replaces the claim.

scopes.original: One mu controls all expectations and a.e. conditions; s is fixed inside each conclusion and outside integrals; matrix identity and matrix zero have their usual meanings.
scopes.reconstructed: The same mu and deterministic s; all integral and matrix summation indices are bound; scalar one is distinguished from matrix identity; no conditional law or random parameter.
scopes.evidence: The reconstruction accurately expands these scopes. Complete P code proves genuine integrability before applying positive integration, avoiding totalized-integral zero defaults. Negative eigenvalues remain unrestricted.

constant_dependencies.original: Fixed zero and one, with identity size determined by I; coefficient exp(s)-s-1 depends only on s; E X squared depends on mu and X.
constant_dependencies.reconstructed: Exactly those dependencies, no unspecified or optimized constant, hidden scale, variance cover or dimension factor.
constant_dependencies.evidence: The source formula and reconstruction constants section contain precisely the P57 coefficient and actual matrix second moment. No new constant-scope dependence is introduced.
